log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp threatens heavy damage against Incineroar, Kingambit, and Gholdengo, making it an excellent lead. Primarina provides a sturdy defensive switch-in against opposing Dragons and Dark types, while Choice Scarf Gholdengo offers critical speed control and cleanup potential.

The opponent has Dragonite, Gholdengo, Mimikyu, Garchomp, Volcarona and Primarina. Dragon types and Fairy types are common, so I want to cover both. Kingambit hits Mimikyu and Gholdengo hard but is weak to Fighting and Fire. Gholdengo is good against Fairy types and Dragons are neutral to it, so it fits. Dragapult is fast and hits Dragonite and Garchomp with Dracometeor, while Fire Blast covers Steel. Garchomp covers Gholdengo and Volcarona with Earthquake and Rock Slide, and it outspeeds most of the field. I'll bring Gholdengo, Dragapult and Garchomp. Incineroar's Intimidate is fine, but the offensive trio fits better against this team.

Dragapult outspeeds the opposing Garchomp, which has at most 169 Speed against my 213. Draco Meteor is super effective and boosted by Life Orb, so it should do heavy damage, likely close to a knockout. Garchomp may Mega Evolve, but that does not change the fact that I move first. Draco Meteor is the strongest option.
Dragapult naturally outspeeds Garchomp and threatens an immediate OHKO with Dragon-type STAB moves. Primarina is immune to Dragon attacks and handles Dragapult very well defensively.

Dragapult outspeeds Primarina and Shadow Ball hits it neutrally. Primarina has Moonblast and Sparkling Aria-type threats, but Dragapult is faster and has Life Orb power. Shadow Ball is the best damage option, and Fire Blast is resisted.
Dragapult's Dragon move failed against Primarina, and Moonblast is a guaranteed OHKO on Dragapult while dealing massive damage to whatever switches in.

Primarina is at 64% and uses Moonblast, which is Fairy. Gholdengo is Steel, so it resists Fairy, and Primarina's Water moves are neutral against it. Gholdengo also has Good as Gold, which blocks status. Makeit Rain is neutral against Primarina but still hurts, and Gholdengo outspeeds it (136 against a max of 123). Garchomp is weak to Fairy and Ice, so Gholdengo is the safer switch.

Gholdengo outspeeds Primarina and has a Focus Sash. Make It Rain is Steel-type, which is super effective against Fairy, and Primarina is at 64%. It should knock out or come very close, and the Sp. Atk drop matters little with a Garchomp still behind. Thunderbolt is super effective too, but Make It Rain hits much harder. Primarina's Moonblast is Fairy and Gholdengo is Steel, so it resists that and takes little damage anyway.
Opposing Gholdengo heavily threatens Primarina with Make It Rain. Switching to Garchomp is safe, as Garchomp resists Steel and easily threatens an OHKO with Earthquake.

Garchomp is at 22% and Gholdengo is at -2 SpA. Shadow Ball is neutral on Garchomp and should still do enough, since 22% is roughly 45 HP. At -2, SpA 203 becomes 101, and Shadow Ball at that level should deal about 25-30%. That's cutting it close, so Make It Rain is the safer pick: Steel is neutral on Dragon/Ground and 120 BP is much stronger, though it drops SpA by another 2. Garchomp may outspeed me and hit first. The Focus Sash is still intact, so I survive one hit and then KO. Make It Rain it is.
Opposing Gholdengo is at 1% HP and Choice Scarf Gholdengo easily outspeeds it to finish it off while preserving Primarina.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
**Analyzing the End Game**

I've just visualized a critical battle scenario. My Garchomp has been knocked out. The opponent's Gholdengo is teetering at 1% health, its Focus Sash now broken. I am envisioning the Gholdengo being choice scarfed, meaning it would easily outspeed and finish the remaining opponent with a Shadow Ball, winning the game in the process.

decisions.thought: Our Choice Scarf ensures we outspeed opposing Gholdengo, and Shadow Ball is a guaranteed 100% accurate knockout to finish it off.

My Gholdengo has 1 HP and is at -4 Sp. Atk, so even a faster Shadow Ball wouldn't threaten a full-HP Gholdengo, and any hit finishes it. Switching to full-HP Garchomp lets it absorb a neutral hit, and it can attack next turn. Gholdengo also comes back later with its boosts reset.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: My Gholdengo is nearly dead with lowered SpA, so switching to Garchomp seems safer since it can tank either of the opponent's Gholdengo attacks and strike back, with Primarina still waiting behind.

decisions.thought: Opposing Gholdengo is at full HP and Earthquake is super effective on it. I outspeed it and Mega Evolving raises Garchomp's attack and its speed. Gholdengo's Shadow Ball is not too threatening, so I should hit hard now. Earthquake with Mega should deal big damage, possibly nearly a knockout, and Rough Skin will chip it as well.
Choice Scarf Gholdengo outspeeds Garchomp and has it down to 51% HP at -1 Special Defense, making Shadow Ball a guaranteed knockout.
My Garchomp fainted, so I have to switch. Gholdengo at 1 HP is the only legal option.
Opposing Gholdengo is at 1% HP, and our Choice Scarf Gholdengo easily outspeeds and secures the knockout with Shadow Ball to win the match.

My Gholdengo is at 1 HP, so it only survives if it moves first or the opponent can't hit it. Shadow Ball is super effective with STAB and is my strongest option, doing roughly 80-100% to their Gholdengo. It probably won't KO, but it might if they have low bulk. I'm likely faster than most of their speed range, so I'll attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Our Gholdengo is down to 1 HP against the opponent's full-health Gholdengo, with Primarina at 64% as our only other option. I'm checking whether the -2 special attack drop still applies to our Gholdengo, but since it switched out for Garchomp earlier, that stat change should have reset.

Comparing moves: Shadow Ball is super effective and should land around 145-171 damage, likely not enough to KO given their HP range, while Thunderbolt is only neutral and weaker. Shadow Ball is clearly the better choice here since protecting won't change the outcome and we need the strongest hit available.
